rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: chunk 9 L83 'The map at sitting 2 had an edge nobody explained' — 'sitting 2' is a numbered-session label that never appears anywhere else in this file's student body, and grepped across the whole AE101 corpus (`grep -rn 'sitting [0-9]'`) it exists ONLY in trainer-facing files (trainer-modules.md, training-architecture.md), never taught to the student. Verified it is not even coincidentally wrong: this section renders only in the no-M6 four-sitting build (`node scripts/check-slide-size.js --training agentic-engineering-101-northwind` lists 'Back to the map, one last time' as a live 192-word slide, absent from the default AE101 build's 11-slide list), and in that exact build M2 (plan-mode-done-right, the only module including lectures/the-whole-map.md, first map reveal) IS trainer-modules.md's documented 'sitting 2' — so the label is not merely internally stable, it is factually correct for its one rendering context. Held as PASS rather than a 'never named' violation because the sentence does not gate comprehension on decoding the ordinal: the figure rendering in the SAME chunk (L81) and the very next clauses ('A dashed line down the right side, THE TEAM beyond it...') fully resolve what the reader needs (the edge, and its explanation) regardless of whether 'sitting 2' itself is decoded — it reads as scene-setting flavor, not a load-bearing referent. Worth a maintainer look (student vocabulary vs. trainer scheduling term) but not a comprehension-blocking failure. All other referents checked: 'the return' (L44/48/72/74, introduced via the chunk-5-closing link title 'Reading the return' before first reuse), 'the kit' (L74-75, arc-earned per `vocabulary.md` 'kit' row, threaded from earn-the-trust/M3, never used in-file before this but legitimately carried per the arc-earned-spine-vocabulary carve-out), 'the gate' (L75, introduced via the chunk-6 link title 'The gate is a claim too' before reuse), 'the loop'/'the map'/'the wall' (all arc-earned per `vocabulary.md`, or named at their own chunk header before reuse), and chunk 7 Key Concepts' 'the public field'/'the local optimum'/'tested-here' (never named earlier in THIS file, but the module's own include-order puts `lectures/what-packaging-is.md` — which teaches all three terms on its mid-deck theory slides, per the maintainer note at the KC block — inline in the composed deck immediately before Key Concepts; this is the module-include-order carve-out applied directly, stronger than the plain arc-earned case since the teaching slide sits earlier in the SAME composed deck, not just an earlier module).

No 'the opening lecture said X' pattern. Chunk 4 L23 'the lecture ahead hands you the lenses' is reading-order language pointing at a link two chunks later (chunk 5 L37 'Reading the return') — a forward promise fulfilled in-file, not a positional pointer whose target shifts with deck-start. Chunk 4 L25 'The M1 countermove' names the source by module + unpacks the claim in the same clause ('tell the agent what output you want') — passes the carve-out's own worked example shape. Chunk 6 L54 'the closing lectures' names two lectures by role and immediately lists them (L57, L59) in the SAME chunk — navigation, not narrative callback, and verified true: 'What packaging is' and 'The gate is a claim too' are in fact the module's last two lecture includes (everything after is metadata/closer/optional, not new lecture content). Chunks 9 and 13 sum the module's own arc, which the rule explicitly allows.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'you have run the loop and built the checks' (L89) and 'the re-send' (L106) point at beats taught earlier in this same file (chunk 6 build-the-check-send-again move; chunk 3 bolded 'Re-send' LO). 'The map at sitting 2 had an edge nobody explained' (L83) points at a beat that verifiably exists: `lectures/the-whole-map.md` is included by `plan-mode-done-right.md` (M2) and its own maintainer note calls it 'M2 open, first map reveal of the training' — the referenced beat is real and current, not stranded by a re-chunk (rule 3's actual test; the ordinal-label clarity concern is filed under rule 1, not here). No 'the X you did' pattern with a dead target found anywhere in body. The removed '## Set up the worktree' section (moved to exercises/fork-the-worktree.md per the maintainer note at L134) left no dangling backward reference — the body only forward-links to the exercise, never assumes the worktree already exists.

Every live chunk carries a self-standing claim or actionable content. Chunk 0 (H1 only, no lede) is the title slide the rule's own preamble defines as prior context for later chunks, not a content chunk needing its own claim. Shortest content chunk is 'Next' (L117-120, 10 words per `check-slide-size.js`) — still states a complete claim about M6. No wait-state or single context-dependent bullet found.

Chunk 9 header 'Back to the map, one last time' (L78) claims this is the final map appearance in the arc. Checked against the corpus: `grep -rln map-engine curriculum/lectures/` shows the figure recurs at M2 (the-whole-map), M3 (the-loop-half-filled), M4 (the-far-half), M5 (this file), AND M6 — `lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` L25-28 '## The checking loop, drawn solid' / `{{figure:map-engine-filled}}`, whose own maintainer note (L88-90) confirms 'the engine map re-shown with the checking loop solid'. Verified via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` that the map's move into composing-the-workflow.md (commit 96fb2a89) predates this file's current judged pin (4589f1d5), so this is not a fresh regression — a standing claim that reads false against the shipped M6 lecture. Harm is mild (the reader isn't misled about anything load-bearing at M5 itself; the mismatch only surfaces if they later notice the map again at M6) and a defensible narrower reading exists ('one last time we come back to the wall/crossing theme', which IS true — M6's map reveal is about the checking loop, not the wall) — filed non-blocking, for the maintainer to either reword the header or confirm the narrower reading is the intended one.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either narrow the header ('Back to the wall, one last time') to match what's actually true, or confirm with the maintainer that the M6 checking-loop reveal doesn't count against 'the map' framing here.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped body for each sub-pattern this session: 'Not X. Not Y. Z' construction — 0 matches; self-grading superlatives ('one of the most', 'most useful/important', 'best way/move/practice') — 0 matches; number+retraction ('about N', 'N%') — 0 matches. Manually scanned for anaphora/epistrophe triples and empty-leg verb triplets: the three-item lists present (goal drift/context rot/plausible-but-wrong L15; the rules file/observations/verifier/reference/plan L87) are technical enumerations used definitionally, not rhetorical repetition of a sentence frame. No abstraction-noun stack found. Closest calls (L35 'the real move is putting the definition in ./CLAUDE.md once', L87 'that is the right order and not a shortfall') are contrastive definitional statements, not training self-praise — stay inside the value-prop-leak boundary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every bulleted chunk (3, 7, 8, 10) and closing prose (9, 13) for the three classes. (a) Doctrine restatement: none found — Key Concepts' four locked lines (L64-67) each state a distinct domain claim, none re-announcing a split/law already stated elsewhere in this file. (b) Self-referential design commentary: none found — no 'you encounter the problems before...' or 'X is by design' predicate-leak anywhere in body. (c) Aphorism kicker: closest calls L87 'That is the right order and not a shortfall: prove it on yourself, then promote' (states a real practice principle, not curriculum self-reference) and L89 'Your call when it's ready' (grants agency without restating the chunk-9 header or a **The point:** line) — both stay inside as voice beats, not koan-kickers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `## Next` is two plain sentences: what the next module does, what the student carries into it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Current `## Next` body (L120) is exactly ONE sentence: 'Module 6 reads the packaged session: subtler misses, subtler drift.' It states what M6 does but never states what the student carries into it, the addendum's required second half. Compared against the corpus's own worked pattern for this exact section: getting-going.md's `## Next` ('Module 2 is where plan mode earns its keep... Your rules file gets read at the top of that session.') and run-the-first-experiment.md's `## Next` ('The next module opens with what came back... You pinned the starting point and recorded where this session lives...') both carry two sentences, module-does then student-carries. M5's is missing the second. Not covered by any maintainer accept-note (grepped the maintainer block for 'Next'/'two sentences' — no hit). Filed non-blocking: the single sentence is still true and self-carrying (rule 6/rule 5 both pass on it independently), this is a completeness gap against the corpus convention, not a comprehension failure.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a second sentence naming what the student carries into M6, e.g. 'You walk in holding both runs of the same task — the diff between them is what M6 reads.'
